audit_findings.title: The cash add-back may include seasonal operating liquidity rather than excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $483.38 million bridge exposure, equal to $2.15 per share and 19.3% of base equity value; the June balance was $84.27 million above December 2025 cash and short-term investments
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds cash and short-term investments directly to equity value; any operating, covenant-bound, or otherwise unavailable portion must be excluded from the add-back.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, cash flow is generally higher in the second quarter as the seasonality of our business peaks and payments are received.
audit_findings.explanation: Seasonality is demonstrated, but the amount of cash required by operations is unresolved. The $551 million of restricted subsidiary net assets does not itself prove that $551 million of cash is restricted. Nevertheless, treating the entire seasonal-peak balance as excess exposes nearly one-fifth of base equity value and is reasonably capable of materially changing intrinsic value.
audit_findings.action: Determine monthly cash and short-term-investment troughs, reconcile the June balance to seasonal receivable collections and liabilities, and obtain covenant calculations identifying the amount legally and practically distributable; rerun the bridge using only demonstrated excess cash.

audit_findings.title: The equity-level OE forecast may retain a temporary interest-hedge benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.6 million of annual pretax interest per 100-basis-point move under the filed December 2025 sensitivity; $600 million of swaps versus $960 million of term debt, with current swaps expiring by March 2028
audit_findings.mechanism: Because OE is measured after interest, future interest expense must reflect swap expirations and the floating-rate debt terms rather than mechanically grow hedge-benefited historical OE.
audit_findings.evidence: A notional amount of $ 100.0 million matures in March 2026, a notional amount of $ 250.0 million matures in January 2027, and a notional amount of $ 250.0 million in March 2028.
audit_findings.explanation: The hedge benefit is demonstrably temporary, although the latest filing shows the $100 million tranche now expiring in March 2027 and the debt was refinanced through 2033 at a lower spread. Future SOFR and replacement-hedge terms are unknown, so the record cannot establish the valuation impact. Failure to reprice would overstate value if post-hedge interest exceeds the expense embedded in the anchor.
audit_findings.action: Build an annual interest schedule through 2033 using the new credit agreement, each current swap maturity, debt amortization, and explicit SOFR cases; rerun equity-level OE and the DCF under those cases.

audit_findings.title: Unaccrued litigation claims may sit ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Uninsured defense, indemnification, settlement, restitution, or governance-remediation payments would reduce OE or require a liability deduction in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: In view of the complexity and ongoing and uncertain nature of the outstanding proceedings and inquiries, at this time we are unable to estimate a reasonably possible range of financial obligation that we may incur to resolve the Derivative Actions.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved contingent claim, not a demonstrated omitted liability. The securities-class-action settlement was separately accrued and paid, while the latest 10-Q reports four derivative actions and still cannot estimate their loss range. Insurance may offset costs, but available limits, retentions, and coverage for derivative claims are not supplied, so materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain current case status, defense-cost accruals, D&O policy limits and remaining limits, retentions, coverage exclusions, indemnification obligations, and any post-filing settlement discussions; rerun the bridge for any probable uninsured amount.

audit_findings.title: The growth path may extrapolate price and acquisition effects as organic growth
audit_findings.magnitude: The 0%-to-6% scenario range changes equity value by $673 million, or $2.99 per share; base exceeds bear by $309 million, or $1.37 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Unsupported growth raises forecast OE and terminal value; acquisition-dependent growth also requires acquisition consideration and associated reinvestment that must be deducted from cash available to owners.
audit_findings.evidence: The Fiscal Year 2025 increase in net sales was primarily driven by positive net price and the favorable impact from acquisitions.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that 2025 sales growth consisted of 5.4% price, 1.1% acquisitions, and no volume growth; first-half 2026 growth consisted mainly of 7.2% price with only 0.4% volume. This does not prove that 3%-6% OE growth is invalid, because pricing can support nominal growth and margins, but the valuation is materially sensitive to the assumption and the record does not show the required organic and acquisition reinvestment.
audit_findings.action: Decompose anchor-period OE changes into volume, price, mix, currency, acquisitions, margins, working capital, and capital expenditure; then rerun each growth case with the corresponding acquisition and operating reinvestment explicitly included.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition-labelled employee compensation must not be normalized away
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.1 million in 2025 and $3.2 million in 2024; the 2025 amount equals 2.2% of the $143.8 million anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding employee-retention compensation back as a nonrecurring acquisition item would overstate historical OE and potentially the trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: The $3.9 million expense in Fiscal Year 2025 primarily included $3.1 million of compensation expenses for the retention of key employees acquired in the ChlorKing acquisition.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the costs were compensation contingent on continued employment, but the supplied record does not establish whether the OE worksheets removed them. Even if the full identified 2025 amount were improperly normalized, it is only 2.2% of anchor OE and occurred within a defined 12-month retention period, which is not large enough on the supplied scale to change the valuation conclusion by itself.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the 2024 and 2025 OE worksheets and restore the $3.2 million and $3.1 million compensation amounts if added back; separately test whether recurring acquisition or restructuring compensation exists beyond the completed ChlorKing retention period.
